sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Personal Electronics and Smart Gadgets

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic-derived Commercial Code with substantial common law influence in maritime, banking, and corporate practice)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement on the Promotion and Protection of Investments between the Government of the Republic of Panama and the Government of the United Mexican States
Agreement between the Republic of Panama and the Kingdom of the Netherlands for the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments
Bilateral Investment Treaty between the Republic of Panama and the Federal Republic of Germany
Investment Trade Promotion Agreement between Panama and the United States (TPA, including investment chapter)
Double Taxation Agreement between Panama and the United Kingdom (signed 2016, pending full ratification status)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Article 1 and Article 4 of Law 70 of May 3, 2019 (creation of the beneficial ownership registry and amendment of Law 23 of April 27, 2015), as implemented by Executive Decree No. 433 of April 29, 2019 and the regulatory resolutions of the Panama Financial Intelligence Unit (UAF); obligatory customer due diligence under Chapter II of Law 23 of 2015.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of the Foundation Charter (Public Instrument)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the jurisdiction where settlor executes the charter (with Panamanian Notary for final execution)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Copy of Beneficial Owner's Passport or National ID
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or Notary Public of owner's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Proof of Address (utility bill or bank statement) for each UBO
Certificate of Good Standing (if settlor is a corporate entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the settlor's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney to the Panamanian Registered Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the grantor's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) screening, OFAC SDN screening, UN Security Council Consoliated List screening, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List screening, and Panamanian UAF 'National List' screening for all settlors, foundation council members, beneficiaries, and their beneficial owners. Screening must be performed at onboarding and continuously for the life of the foundation under Law 23 of 2015 and the regulations of the UAF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Oficina Virtual (Public Registry of Panama – Online Name Reservation Module at www.registro-publico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All legal entities must be registered in Spanish; foreign names must be transliterated into Latin alphabet phonetically and adapted to Spanish grammar. Any identical or phonetically identical name to any existing registered entity in the Registro Público is automatically rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File a written petition with the Sub-Directorate of the Mercantile Registry of the Public Registry within 5 business days of rejection, providing supporting evidence of distinctiveness (e.g., trademark registration, prior use, or consent of the previously registered entity). If rejected again, file an administrative reconsideration before the Director General of the Public Registry within 15 days; an ultimate appeal may be filed with the Fiscal (Administrative) Litigation Chamber of the Supreme Court within two months of the final administrative decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office address is permitted solely as the registered agent's address for service of process and administrative notifications. For an e-commerce retainer engaged in taxable commercial activities, the foundation must maintain underlying substance such as personnel or data-decision infrastructure; a purely virtual registered office with no commercial activity in Panama may expose the foundation to tax-residency and substance challenges under Panama's economic substance and territorial tax rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate for retail e-commerce if virtual office only; estimated annual probability of unannounced inspection by the Panamanian Tax Administration (DGI) or the UAF for a low-risk e-commerce foundation is approximately 10%, depending on payment-volume triggers and cross-border transaction patterns.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Precio de los Servicios del Registro Público (D.S. No. 4 de 1989, as amended)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the foundation public deed and related affidavits
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff for first ten pages, approximately USD 75 per deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille authentication of UBO and settlor documents (per document, estimated 5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the country of apostille (Panama or issuing jurisdiction)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Panama's fee schedule under Law 30 of 2000 and Hague Convention implementing regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registry filing fee for Private Interest Foundation incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Incorporation fee for foundation charter filing under the Public Registry tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Economy and Finance / Panama Financial Intelligence Unit (UAF)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Nominal administrative fee for beneficial ownership registry access and submission

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent service fee and registered office for first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Panamanian registered agent (law firm or corporate services provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for low-risk single-foundation structure in Panama City

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening (settlor + foundation council + beneficiaries)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial standard fee for beneficial ownership screening of three individuals

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal analysis and document drafting (custom foundation charter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Pre-approved fixed fee for foundation formation and AML due-diligence pack, typical market range

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended by Ley 41 de 2013; Articles 3, 5-10 and 16-19; Reglamento del Registro Público, Book VII, Foundations Section; DGI Beneficial Ownership Resolutions under Law 41/2013.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter / Deed of Constitution, including its internal Regulations)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Mandatory initial endowment of at least US$10,000.00 (Law 25/1995, Art. 8). The endowment may be declared as fully subscribed in the Charter and recorded in the foundations ledger; no escrow deposit or physical capitalization is required, but the endowment must be stated in Balboas/USD and supported by a contribution declaration; deficiency must be cured by the Foundation Council before distribution of benefits.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the Founder's declaration establishing the Private Interest Foundation's initial endowment of Ten Thousand United States Dollars (US$10,000.00) is ratified, fully subscribed and recorded as contributed in the Foundation Charter. RESOLVED FURTHER: that the registered office located at (Panama City address) is adopted, and the designation of (Registered Agent) is confirmed. RESOLVED FURTHER: that the Foundation Council is appointed as follows: (Name), President; (Name), Secretary; (Name), Treasurer, each acting severally with the powers granted by the Foundation Charter and Law 25 of 1995. RESOLVED FURTHER: that the Supervisory Body, (Protector name), is appointed. The undersigned Council President is hereby authorized to execute all registry filings, bank arrangements, and lease agreements required to commence lawful operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Services Portal (Servicio de Certificado de Nombre / Reserva de Nombre)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed distinctive names bearing the mandatory suffix 'Fundación de Interés Privado'. The request must be filed electronically with a certified Panamanian counsel or directly through the registros public portal. Upon approval, the name reservation certificate is valid for a statutory period during which the Charter must be presented; any delay requires renewal before registration.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application (form AP-101)
Certificate of incorporation of corporate founder (if any), apostilled or legalized
Founder's identification copies (passport or state-issued ID)
Power of attorney for the submitting counsel (PN-issued)
Name reservation fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any proposed name is refused for misleading similarity or prohibited terms, file an amended request with alternative names; a formal refusal may be contested through Recurso de Reconsideración before the Registro General within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría del Circuito del Distrito de Panamá (Circuit Notary Public)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder (or authorized representative) executes before the Notary the Foundation Charter in Spanish, including the endowment declaration, registered agent acceptance, Foundation Council members' acceptance, and the internal Regulations. The instrument must expressly state the foundation's commercial object covering online retail of personal electronics (ISIC 4791) and smart gadgets, per Law 25 Article 6, to avoid ultra vires challenges. The Notary verifies the identity, capacity, and AML screening of all signatories, then issues the protocolized deed for registry submission.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate issued by Registro Público
Draft Foundation Charter and internal Regulations (Spanish)
Registered Agent acceptance letter and legal representation certificate
Passport copies and Tax Information (n/a) declarations of founder and council members
AML/KYC questionnaires for all officers (per Law 23/2015 and Superintendency rules)
Original fee payment receipts for notarial services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary identifies defects, the Charter is re-drafted and re-executed without penalty; any notarial refusal is appealable to the Judicial Branch (Juzgado) under the Notarial Regulation Decree.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation Charter at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Private Interest Foundations Section)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The protocolized Charter (certified copy) is filed for inscription together with the certified name certificate and registered agent's accepted appointment. The Registry examiners verify compliance with Law 25/1995 Articles 7-10 and Book VII of the Registry Regulation, including the endowment figure, object clause, council composition, and registered agent legitimacy. Upon approval, the foundation acquires distinct legal personality; an expedited (fast-track) procedure is available for a surcharge.
required_dossiers: Authenticated/certified copy of the notarial Foundation Charter
Original name reservation certificate
Registered Agent acceptance deed
Registry fee payment voucher (graduated by capital: approx. USD 250 + surcharges if expedited)
Certified translation (Spanish) if any exhibit is in another language
Identification copy of the registered agent's attorney (if entity agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry returns a caveat (calificación desfavorable), counsel has 10 business days to correct defects and re-present; rejection may be challenged via Recurso de Apelación before the Director General del Registro Público.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Ownership Registry Filing and RUC Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – Beneficial Ownership Registry and Taxpayer Registry (RUC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 calendar days of foundation inscription, file the Beneficial Ownership (BO) Declaration with DGI under Law 41/2013 and ITS DGI-SET resolution, disclosing founder, council members, protector, and ultimate beneficiaries. Concurrently obtain the RUC identification number for the foundation. The RUC and BO records are used for territorial tax compliance, the annual US$300 flat franchise tax, and payment processor onboarding. A territorial tax status certificate (aviso de operación de comercio electrónico under the DGI single window) is issued thereafter.
required_dossiers: Public Registry issuance certificate of the foundation
Qualified BO declaration form (Form 0421/current DGI BO form)
Passport copies and physical address of each BO and officer
Lease agreement or ownership deed of Panama registered office
RUC application (Form R-100) and appointing a fiscal domicile
Registered agent's certification as to BO veracity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late BO filing penalties (up to USD 5,000) may be mitigated by voluntary self-correction before DGI; for RUC issues, submit an administrative aclaración and, if rejected, appeal to the Tribunal Administrativo Tributario within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Operation Permit (Aviso de Operación) for E-Commerce Retail
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía del Distrito de Panamá – Ventanilla Única de Inversión (Municipal Single Investment Window) / Panama Emprende Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Aviso de Operación (Municipal Business Operation Permit) under ISIC 4791, specifying online retail of personal electronics and smart gadgets. Provide the RUC, registered office lease, fire-safety inspection certificate, and DGI compliance status. The permit is granted as a municipal activity certificate that must be renewed annually, and is required by processing platforms (including Stripe/PayPal) to evidence lawful merchant existence.
required_dossiers: RUC registration certificate
Certified copy of foundation Charter and Public Registry inscription
Registered office lease or proprietary title (certified by a public notary)
Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (Dirección General de Bomberos)
Municipal tax clearance and payment of the municipal license fee (typically USD 50-200 based on category)
Identity documents of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried, correct the cited deficiencies within 15 days under the Ventanilla Única; final municipal refusal can be appealed through Administrative Recourse of Reconsideration and, if needed, annulment action before the Contencioso Administrativo Tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Consumer Protection E-Commerce Registration and Payment Rails Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Autoridad de Protección al Consumidor y Defensa de la Competencia (ACODECO) – Electronic Commerce Unit; and Payment Processor compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the e-commerce establishment's terms, returns policy, and data-processing notices with ACODECO as applicable, and implement the mandatory consumer complaint channel (Ley 45/2011 and E-Commerce regulations). Concurrently complete Stripe and PayPal onboarding by submitting the Panamanian foundation's KYC pack: certified Charter, RUC, Aviso de Operación, bank reference letter, and identification of beneficial owners. Confirm that PCI-DSS compliance is documented for handling card data under the Superintendency of Banks rules.
required_dossiers: Aviso de Operación and RUC certificates (certified copies)
Foundation Charter with object clause covering e-commerce (ISIC 4791)
ACODECO e-commerce registration form and privacy notice template
Payment processor application forms (Stripe/PayPal) with BO schema
Compliance attestation (AML/KYC) for the Foundation Council
Registered office address proof and operational email/domain registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ACODECO flags consumer terms, amend the online policies promptly and re-submit; for payment processor rejection, supply an alternative bank-account verification or certified translation of documents and escalate to the processor's KYB team.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – including the Dirección de Empresas; Municipal license authority: Alcaldía del Distrito de Panamá
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación de Comercio Electrónico (Municipal E-Commerce Business Operation Permit) combined with the MICI Electronic Commerce Activity Registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Verificación del Desempeño Ambiental (DIVEDA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Environmental Registration (Registro de Actividad de Impacto Ambiental No Significativo) – no full EIA required for ISIC 4791 online retail warehousing; environmental compliance certificate is issued upon registration, subject to annual renewal.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary-wastewater discharge limited to municipal sewer standards (pH 6.0-9.0, BOD5 ≤ 200 mg/L, TSS ≤ 220 mg/L); no industrial process water allowed; e-waste, spent batteries, and defective electronics must be segregated and surrendered to MiAMBIENTE-authorized collection recyclers under Law 33 of 2018 (Integrated Waste Management) and the national e-waste rules; packaging and expanded polystyrene prohibited in the City of Panama paid-consumer bags pursuant to municipal ordinance; no VOC or atmospheric emissions are permitted from storage operations, and ODS refrigerants are prohibited in accordance with the Montreal Protocol national implementation; the facility must keep a waste-composition log for inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Dirección General de Bomberos de Panamá issuance of the Certificado de Inspección de Bomberos (annual fire-safety inspection covering electrical routes, fire extinguishers, and egress signage for the retail/warehousing unit); Dirección de Obras y Construcciones de la Alcaldía de Panamá issuance of the structural-load compliance and updated occupancy clearance (Certificado de Estructura y Uso) for the leased premises; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) registration of the workplace health-and-safety committee and occupational hazard prevention plan for any employees, per the DSHA regulations, including ergonomic standards for e-commerce pick-pack zones and general civil-defense clearance for emergency evacuation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; online services through Sede Electrónica at www.dgi.gob.pa and the SIF electronic invoicing platform (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned or non-resident-founded Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) from DGI. Procedure: (1) appoint a Panamanian licensed attorney or firm as resident agent; (2) register the foundation's public deed and articles of incorporation with DGI through the authorized agent; (3) declare the fiscal domicile in Panama and the primary economic activity code corresponding to ISIC 4791 (online retail); (4) request the RUC certificate and, if Panamanian territorial operations exist, simultaneous ITBMS registration; (5) obtain an electronic signature credential for SIF/e-filing. The nominal foundation endowment required by Law 25 of 1995 is satisfied by the statutory minimum of USD 10,000 declared in the foundation deed; no capital payment or deposit is required for tax registration purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope: The PIF is a separate juridical person and a separate taxable person. It is not a pass-through entity. Under Panama's territorial income tax (ISR), only income whose source is located in Panama is taxable. Foreign-source e-commerce receipts (online sales of consumer electronics to non-residents, with delivery and use outside Panama) fall outside the Panamanian territorial nexus. Income derived from activities carried out in Panama, including local stock, logistics, or fulfillment operations, would be Panamanian-source and subject to ISR at the standard corporate rate; Law 25 of 1995 additionally grants PIFs exemption from national taxes within its statutory scope, subject to DGI interpretation for active commercial activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None applicable. Panama does not provide check-the-box classification elections comparable to the United States, and has not implemented OECD BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch rules. The territorial source regime is mandatory and cannot be opted out of; no election is available to treat foreign-source income as taxable or to claim pass-through treatment for a PIF.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), a VAT-type transfer tax under the Panamanian Código Fiscal.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general numeric ITBMS registration threshold: any person performing taxable transfers of goods or services in Panama, or importing goods for sale, must obtain RUC and ITBMS registration. The simplified Small Taxpayer Regime (Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente) applies to taxpayers with annual gross income of B/. 300,000 or less (Balboas, at parity with USD), allowing reduced filing obligations. Pure offshore e-commerce sales with no Panamanian inventory, fulfillment, or local buyer nexus do not trigger ITBMS registration or taxation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing through the DGI's SIF (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica). Taxpayers carrying out taxable activities in Panama must issue e-invoices using SIF or DGI-approved software integrated via web-service API; invoices are transmitted to DGI in near-real-time and must carry a unique DGI authorization number. No physical ink stamp or fiscal seal is applied to electronic invoices; the electronic XML record is the controlling evidence. Non-electronic paper invoices require prior DGI authorization and may be used only in excepted cases.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The ITBMS 0% rate applies to: (a) goods physically exported from Panama, including distance/online retail sales of consumer electronics delivered abroad to non-resident buyers; (b) services rendered to non-residents and effectively used or consumed outside Panama; and (c) sales into Panamanian Zonas Francas. The seller must hold an active ITBMS registration if it maintains Panamanian operations, must issue a compliant SIF e-invoice with the export zero-rating code, and must prove that the goods left Panamanian territory and the buyer is a non-resident. For a PIF with no Panamanian logistics, the underlying income is foreign-source and outside the ISR territorial base; export zero-rating is only invoked where goods are physically shipped from Panama and the seller has a Panamanian ITBMS registration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DUA (Declaración Única Aduanera) export declaration duly validated and sealed by the Panama Customs Authority (ANA) through the SIA/SIGA single-window system
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the e-invoice issued through SIF
Transport document evidencing physical departure from Panama: ocean Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or courier consignment note (DHL, FedEx, UPS)
Inward remittance certificate or bank credit advice showing payment settlement from the foreign buyer's account
Evidence of non-residence of the buyer: overseas billing address, shipping destination, and IP/geolocation records for the online transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama has no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day period is the DGI-benchmarked substantiation standard for export transactions and foreign-source income treatment. Failure to substantiate an export within DGI's documentary requirements results in reassessment of ITBMS at 7% plus statutory interest and surcharges, alongside administrativemonetary penalties under Código Fiscal Articles 759 through 762, which may reach 100% of the omitted tax. Fraudulent or sham export documentation, including false DUAs, backdated bills of lading, or fabricated remittance certificates, triggers criminal tax fraud prosecution under Articles 802 and following of the Código Fiscal, retrospective clawback for up to five fiscal years, nullification of the zero-rating position, and potential suspension of the PIF's RUC and the resident agent's license.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama maintains no conventional central bank and consequently no domestic monetary authority setting reserve requirements or exchange-rate policy. The Republic is fully dollarized: the US dollar is legal tender and circulates alongside the Panamanian balboa, which exists only as fractional coinage at a fixed 1:1 parity. Banking supervision and prudential regulation are vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) under Legislative Decree 2 of 2008 (amending Law 9 of 1998). Banco Nacional de Panamá performs limited fiscal-agency, government-cash-management, and clearing-house functions, while AML/CFT supervision of non-financial sectors falls under the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and Law 23 of 2015.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility applies to both current-account and capital-account transactions. Because the USD is legal tender and the PAB is a purely nominal unit, there is no separate exchange rate to administer, no surrender requirement, and no capital-control authorization regime. E-commerce receipts from Stripe and PayPal settle in USD without an intermediary conversion. Profit remittance, founder capital injections, distributions to foundation council members or beneficiaries, and payments to foreign suppliers are unrestricted, subject only to bank-level source-of-funds verification and suspicious-transaction reporting. For the Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF), which is tax-classified under a territorial model, foreign-source income from cross-border online retail is not subject to Panamanian income tax, and capital can be freely accumulated or distributed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. There is no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no export-proceeds surrender obligation in Panama. Export earnings generated through digital marketplaces settle in USD, which is the lawful circulating currency, so 100% of proceeds may be retained, reinvested, or disbursed without Central Bank-style approval. The only compliance overlay is the territorial tax rule: revenue derived from foreign-market consumer sales is generally foreign-source income exempt from Panamanian income tax, provided the PIF does not maintain a permanent establishment in Panama; the applicability should be confirmed with the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) for ITBMS treatment of physically delivered gadgets.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_and_current_account_policy_descr: Open capital account; dollarized economy; zero exchange-rate risk for USD-denominated treasury operations; no capital-flow restrictions affecting PIF seed capital or profit distribution.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW. Panama has no specialist electronic-money-institution (EMI) licensing regime analogous to UK FCA e-money licenses or Lithuanian EMI authorizations; bank-account opening for a corporate foundation requires an SBP-licensed commercial bank. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise Business, Mercury, Payoneer, Airwallex) generally classify Panama-domiciled Private Interest Foundations as high-structure risk, require physical or substantive regional nexus, or reject them outright because the PIF lacks a licensed-entity status recognized by the EMI's third-party compliance stack. Legal constraints: Law 23 of 2015 and SBP general regulations require the PIF to identify all authorized signatories and beneficial owners through a DGI-registered beneficial-ownership declaration; EMIs unable to access the Panamanian Beneficial Ownership Registry typically decline onboarding. Additionally, the target payment rails (Stripe, PayPal) serve as the PSP layer, and funds ultimately must clear into a domestic banking account; therefore the optimal structure is a PAN-licensed bank as master settlement account with Stripe/PayPal as acquirer gateways, not an offshore EMI as treasury home.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in practice for at least one authorized person. The foundation's resident agent or an authorized signatory must be physically present in Panama for the account-opening interview at the majority of tier-1 institutions, including Banco General and Banistmo; BAC Credomatic and Multibank accept a remote initial interview only where the PIF appoints a Panama-based attorney-in-fact via notarized and apostilled power of attorney. The KYC protocol requires the foundation council members and resolvers to provide certified passport copies, professional reference letters, source-of-wealth statements, and evidence of the foundation's registered address and business purpose. For a non-resident council, an apostilled POA designating a Panamanian law firm or licensed fiduciary as local agent is permitted; however, a purely remote account opening for a new e-commerce foundation with non-resident controllers is generally rejected at first-pass underwriting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF is newly registered under Law 25 of 1995 with no financial statements, no operating history, and high projected transaction velocity from international consumer e-commerce, triggering the bank's 'new vehicle with no audit trail' red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the foundation charter and bylaws (registered in the Registro Público de Panamá); foundation council resolution authorizing account opening and designating signatories; detailed business plan covering ISIC 4791 online electronics retail; executed merchant agreements with Stripe and PayPal; proof of inventory procurement (pro-forma invoices from suppliers, logistics contracts); initial 90-day cash-flow projection; source-of-funds letter and bank reference from the founder's bank of record; certificate of good standing and professional reference from the resident agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Confidential-beneficiary structure of the PIF creates apparent UBO opacity; the bank flags the absence of named beneficiaries under AML risk-rating in accordance with Law 23 of 2015 and DGI Beneficial Ownership regulations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written voluntary waiver of foundation confidentiality executed by the founder and council; private instrument naming the beneficiaries or, alternatively, a declaration that the foundation acts as an asset-holding vehicle for the founder as ultimate beneficial owner; DGI beneficial-ownership filing confirmation (Form 940/beneficial-owner registry acknowledgment); notarized statements of source of wealth; criminal-record certificates from country of residence; professional references from two regulated institutions (bank/attorney/CPA).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment processor pass-through risk: the bank perceives that marketplace settlement from Stripe/PayPal into the PIF account could be used for collection-and-payout layering without genuine commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Direct merchant-account statements from Stripe and PayPal evidencing the PIF as the named merchant; authenticated platform integration screenshots; chargeback and refund policies; sample sales invoices with traceable order IDs; shipping and delivery documentation (courier tracking, customs forms); annual/quarterly management accounts certified by a Panamanian CPA; operating procedures manual demonstrating end-to-end goods flow; compliance declaration that the account serves only as settlement destination, not as a pass-through conduit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Territorial-tax ambiguity: the bank queries whether the offshore-sourced e-commerce income is properly declared and whether the PIF maintains tax registration, triggering 'fiscal transparency' due-diligence flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) tax-identification certificate; Aviso de Operación commercial-license notification (if applicable); DGI tax-registration status certificate; territorial-income legal opinion from a Panamanian tax attorney confirming exemption of foreign-source digital-commerce sales; declaration of non-engagement in Panama-source activities; recent utility/title/lease evidence for registered office; confirmation of ITBMS handling for any local input purchases or advisory services.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: the founder remits seed capital via SWIFT MT103 from the founder's own external bank account to the PIF's USD account at the selected Panamanian bank. Payment narrative must state: 'Capital endowment - Private Interest Foundation [legal name]' or 'Aportación de capital inicial - Fundación [legal name]', accompanied by a board-of-council resolution authorizing receipt of the endowment. The bank's compliance unit will require a source-of-funds letter, proof of the founder's identity, and the DGI beneficial-ownership declaration made prior to first credit. Because Panama has no exchange-control filing, no central-bank license or purpose-code approval is required; however, the wire must not be split to avoid round-sum treatment, and cash deposits above USD 10,000 trigger STR reporting under UAF rules. For a foundation whose charter sets a minimum capital, the injection should equal or exceed that stated capital, with the constitution act referencing the payment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 serial payments for pre-paid T/T settlements to electronics suppliers in China and APAC; (2) Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) issued by the Panamanian bank under UCP 600 for container-volume procurement from verified vendors; (3) direct USD clearings through US correspondent banks (e.g., JPMorgan Chase, Citibank, or Bank of America correspondent networks used by Banco General/BAC/Banistmo) to final beneficiary accounts; (4) PSP settlement inbound rails from Stripe and PayPal, which aggregate consumer card payments and deposit net proceeds in USD into the PIF operational account; (5) for CNY-denominated supplier invoices where USD settlement is not available, a fee-based conversion through the bank's FX desk (spot USD/CNH) or a binding NDF is used, with the underlying trade contract evidenced to the FX desk. No documentary LC is required for parcel-level e-commerce supply; a stand-by LC may be used to collateralize a Chinese trading-company credit line where the PIF desires open-account terms.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/CNY non-deliverable forward (NDF) executed through an SBP-licensed Panamanian bank or an international counterparty with a recognized dealing capability (settlement in USD regardless of CNY movement)
Deliverable USD/EUR outright forward for European inventory sourcing, with standard ISDA 1998 or CSA documentation where applicable
USD/CNH deliverable forward contracts via correspondent branch network for vendors able to receive CNY
Cross-currency swap (USD to EUR or CNY) for term-matched liquidity hedging of fixed procurement commitments
Plain-vanilla FX options (USD calls/puts on CNY or EUR) for conditional procurement pipelines, permitted without regulatory pre-approval
Zero-cost collar structures combining a put and call on USD/CNY where vendor payment timing is uncertain

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Payment of the annual franchise tax (Tasa Única) on the foundation's RUC record, evidenced by the DGI payment voucher required to obtain the Paz y Salvamento (good-standing certificate).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; collected through the licensed resident agent's DGI online portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: June 30 of each calendar year; flat USD 300 per PIF without proration for mid-year incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late surcharge plus 1.5% monthly interest on arrears; loss of Paz y Salvamento; suspension of the foundation's DGI registration and, after repeated consecutive defaults, administrative dissolution or cancellation at the request of the DGI.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO register declaration (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales) - event-driven updates and the resident agent's annual KYC accuracy confirmation of beneficial ownership data.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI - Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF), accessible exclusively by the licensed resident agent.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Update within 15 calendar days of any change in the foundation council, protector, settlor's reserved powers, or beneficiary entitlements; annual accuracy confirmation aligned with the June 30 franchise-tax cycle; no filing is due in a year without changes.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of up to USD 5,000 per violation and USD 500 per day of continued non-compliance after an official DGI requirement; knowingly false UBO information is a criminal offense under Law 23 of 2015 (as amended) and may trigger the resident agent's resignation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Income-tax declaration (Declaración de Renta) - conditional obligation applying only if the PIF realizes Panamanian-source taxable income; the standard asset-holding PIF with foreign-source assets files no periodic corporate return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year (March 31 for a December 31 year-end), only if Panamanian-source taxable income was realized; otherwise the PIF merely maintains its annual franchise tax receipt and Paz y Salvamento.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If triggered, late filing exposes the foundation to a 10% surcharge on the omitted tax plus 1.5% monthly interest under the Fiscal Code, loss of Paz y Salvamento, and blocking of Public Registry acts; zero-activity PIFs without Panamanian-source income incur no DGI filing penalty.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit of a Private Interest Foundation is imposed by Law 25 of 1995 solely because of its legal form; the DGI may require audited financial statements under the Fiscal Code where the foundation itself engages in business in Panama with annual gross receipts above USD 1,000,000, and banks or regulated counterparties may contractually require an independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the Colegio de Contadores Públicos de Panamá and accepted by the DGI; a passive asset-holding PIF commonly applies simplified cash-basis records acceptable to the DGI, with full IFRS or IFRS for SMEs used whenever audited statements are prepared.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 23 of 2015 and Executive Decree No. 213 of 2018, the resident agent must keep the foundation's beneficial-ownership register on the DGI electronic portal and identify the ultimate natural persons controlling the foundation (settlor, protector if vested with powers, and foundation council members) together with any designated beneficiaries by class; any amendment to the foundation charter, substitute council member, protector change, or transfer of foundation interests must be reported to the RBF portal within 15 calendar days; the agent performs an annual KYC/UBO refresh at the franchise-tax cycle to confirm continuing accuracy, and no public annual return is delivered to the Public Registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Protocolized foundation charter with the Public Registry certificate of registration
Resident agent's UBO register maintained under Law 23 of 2015

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - 1,500 per annum for licensed resident agent, registered office, UBO register administration and franchise-tax processing
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - 4,000 per engagement for a certified audit of a simple passive asset-holding PIF by a Panamanian CPA firm when contractually or administratively required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (progressive schedule per Law 134 of 2023: 19% on taxable income up to PAB 50,000; 24% on income from PAB 50,001 to PAB 1,500,000; 25% on income exceeding PAB 1,500,000; the Panamanian Balboa is pegged 1:1 to the US dollar, which circulates as legal tender)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: only Panama-source income is taxable; foreign-source income from cross-border e-commerce sales is excluded if the activities, delivery, and contracting occur outside Panama. Optional Multinational Company Headquarters (SEM) regime may reduce effective CIT to 5% on qualified Panama-source income, and export-oriented activities may benefit from specific promotion regimes, but no general tax holiday applies to online consumer-electronics retail.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 400 (Declaración de Renta Anual) filed through the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) E-TAX 2.0 electronic system (https://etax.dgi.gob.pa); obligatory for all legal entities including Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) that hold a Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal year generally the calendar year; additional bi-annual advance income tax returns are required under the 'Anticipo de Renta' rules).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within four months after the close of the fiscal year. A calendar-year taxpayer must file no later than 30 April of the following year; no automatic extension exists, but a formally justified extension may be obtained from the DGI before the due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number (RUC), full legal name of the Private Interest Foundation, and covered fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PIF must register with the DGI through an authorized resident agent or registered public accountant; the non-resident founder/beneficiary is not named as taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Primary economic activity code and description; this scope corresponds to ISIC 4791 (online retail of personal electronics and smart gadgets).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter exact CIIU 4791; inaccurate activity codes may trigger profit-recharacterization audits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and service revenue net of discounts, returns, and allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Panama-source sales are included; overseas consumer sales sourced outside Panama are segregated as foreign-source revenue and supported by shipping and payment records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income excluded from taxable gross income under the territoriality principle.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Strict documentation of the transaction chain (supplier location, delivery terms, fulfilment centre, acceptance of orders) is required to rebut DGI assertions of Panama source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Inventory cost and directly attributable fulfilment/shipping costs for goods sold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibility depends on arm's-length pricing with related suppliers; cross-border related-party purchases above USD 5,000,000 must be supported by a transfer-pricing study.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income determined after allowed deductible expenses attributable to Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent or beneficiary general-and-administrative expenses are deductible only with true economic substance and proper intercompany agreements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 160-180 – ISR Causado / Retenciones / Saldo por Pagar
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed corporate income tax, application of withheld amounts and advance credits, and final balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any final tax due must be paid no later than the filing deadline; payment is generally made in US dollars; underpayment generates surcharges and daily interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and late payment attract a surcharge (recargo) of 20% of the tax due plus monthly interest on arrears; additional DGI fines for incomplete returns range from USD 100 to USD 5,000; non-filing for three consecutive years may trigger administrative closure of the RUC, suspension of the PIF's registration, and criminal tax-evasion exposure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% dividend withholding tax on distributions made out of Panama-source profits that have been subject to corporate tax (Article 731, Fiscal Code); distributions sourced from foreign-source exempt reserves are not subject to dividend WHT if properly evidenced; Law 134 of 2023 introduces reduced rates (5%) for certain small-taxpayer distributions within defined brackets.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has a limited but expanding network of double tax agreements (e.g., United Kingdom, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Mexico, South Korea, Singapore, France, Netherlands, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Luxembourg, Switzerland). To obtain treaty-reduced dividend withholding (typically 5% on qualifying direct shareholdings), the non-resident beneficial owner must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and certificate of beneficial ownership from the residence state; (2) submit these together with DGI Form 'Solicitud de Beneficio de Convenio' and the Panamanian payer's certification to the DGI; (3) receive a DGI administrative clearance before the dividend distribution date; and (4) preserve records for five years. Without pre-approved DGI clearance, the payer must withhold the full 10% statutory rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Panamanian withholding on payments to non-residents: 12.5% on interest sourced in Panama (with exemptions for certain international financing and registered securities) and 15% on royalties and technical-service fees; applicable treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 5-10% and royalties to 10%, subject to the same DGI clearance protocol and to the limitation-on-benefits provisions of each treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 5,000,000 (US dollar/Balboa). A taxpayer whose related-party transactions in a fiscal year exceed USD 5,000,000 must file Form 430 (Declaración Informativa de Precios de Transferencia) and prepare a full transfer-pricing study. Entities belonging to multinational groups with consolidated revenue exceeding USD 135,000,000 must additionally prepare a Master File and Local File; Country-by-Country reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue exceeding USD 750,000,000 under OECD-aligned rules.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Panamanian Economic Substance Act (Law 254 of 2019; Executive Decree 345 of 2019) applies to legal entities, including PIFs, that carry on 'relevant activities' in or from Panama. Online retail conducted through a Panamanian distribution centre or with staff soliciting, negotiating, or concluding contracts in Panama will be classified as a 'distribution and service centre' and will require local substance, including a local office, qualified personnel, and direction of core income-generating activities in Panama. A purely passive PIF holding foreign e-commerce contracts and receiving book-outsourced revenue outside Panama is not subject to ESR; however, the DGI may disregard artificial arrangements that lack substance and recharacterize them as Panama-source.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission, concealment, or false characterization of online consumer-electronics sales as foreign-source income when fulfilment, logistics, or contracting activities are actually conducted in Panama; submission of fraudulent Form 400 declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil surcharge of up to 50%-150% of the evaded tax, plus interest; criminal tax-fraud penalties include imprisonment of 2 to 5 years, increased to up to 12 years for aggravated offences involving multiple schemes or large values; applicable fine of USD 5,000 to USD 50,000 or more depending on tax amount involved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, Foundation Council members, and the resident agent who knowingly sign false returns or consent to the omission are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, surcharges, and penalties; courts may pierce the corporate veil, impose asset embargoes and travel bans, and order personal criminal custody.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a PIF without office, staff, economic activity, or decision-making in Panama, while routing e-commerce income through the foundation solely to avoid tax in another jurisdiction, or maintaining the foundation's registration purely as a corporate facade.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic Substance Regulations administrative fines of USD 15,000 to USD 25,000 per violation and per year; repeat violations can trigger deregistration of the foundation, nullification of its acts, and reassessment of taxes for up to five prior years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members and the fiduciary who falsely certify substance reports are personally liable for fines; fraudulent simulation may expose beneficial owners to anti-money-laundering prosecution with forfeiture of assets and criminal penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form 430, failure to prepare a Transfer Pricing Study or Master/Local File when related-party transactions exceed USD 5,000,000, or use of a non-arm's-length pricing arrangement with foreign suppliers or a related payment processor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may adjust the taxable base upward, apply a 20% surcharge on the adjusted tax, and impose fines up to USD 5,000 for failure to file informative returns; daily interest continues to accrue until settlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who disregard TP obligations after written DGI notice may be personally liable for the reassessed tax and fines; malicious cross-border transfer pricing that shifts taxable profits abroad is treated as tax fraud and can lead to criminal indictment and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing earnings or value to a non-resident beneficiary or founder without withholding the statutory 10% dividend tax or without obtaining treaty-relief clearance, or disguising dividends as loans, management fees, or IP royalty payments to avoid WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The PIF is liable for the withheld tax and becomes subject to a 20% surcharge plus interest; false characterization of dividends as deductible fees triggers disallowance, a double economic tax charge, and fines of up to USD 10,000; criminal sanctions apply for fraudulent repatriation schemes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members and the resident agent who authorize unauthorized distributions or knowingly mischaracterize cross-border payments are personally liable for the deficiency; the DGI may impose personal asset embargoes, exit bans, and, in money-laundering-connected cases, up to 12 years' imprisonment.
